title: SLO decomposition for mixed-latency endpoints and adaptive rollout criteria
creator: Asha Nambiar
description:
Problem: We lack a decomposed SLO surface that reflects mixed-latency workloads (streaming chat, interactive non-streaming, embeddings) and an explicit adaptive rollout policy that ties error budget burn to graduated canary expansion. This ticket is a product-level PRD to: 1) define per-endpoint/per-profile SLO targets (p50/p95/p99 + availability), 2) establish error budget accounting rules (per-tenant and global), and 3) specify automated rollout gates and thresholds for progressive releases (canary -> ramp -> global).

Goals:
- Produce a clear SLO matrix for Hosted API endpoints that maps to runtime rollout controls and observability dashboards.
- Define acceptable degradation bands and automated actions when error budgets burn (throttle, fallback to cheaper model variants, pause rollout).
- Create testable acceptance criteria and concrete gating rules implementable by infra/console teams.

Scope:
- Included: Hosted API endpoints (chat streaming, chat non-streaming, embeddings, rerank), tiered per-tenant SLO tagging (standard vs. premium), definitions of burn-rate windows and canary expansion logic.
- Excluded: Dedicated capacity contractual SLAs, Private/VPC-specific network SLOs, and legal/contract wording (handled by contracts team).

Approach:
- Draft SLO matrix (see acceptance_criteria).
- Collaborate with Eng to map SLO signals to alerting and gating hooks (burn rate, progressive rollback automation).
- Add dashboard templates and a Confluence playbook for on-call/runbook triggers.
acceptance_criteria: SLO matrix completed and agreed by Eng/DR/OBS: interactive-chat (hosted, streaming): p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 500ms, p99 <= 1200ms; availability >= 99.95% monthly.
Embeddings endpoint (hosted): p50 <= 30ms, p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 350ms; availability >= 99.97% monthly.
Rerank/batched endpoints: p50 <= 180ms, p95 <= 800ms, p99 <= 1800ms; availability >= 99.9% monthly.
Error budget accounting defined: per-tenant rolling 7-day and 30-day windows plus a global monthly budget; specify conversion between latency violations and error-budget units for mixed signals.

Rollout gates specified: initial canary max 5% of traffic for 24h with burn-rate check (<= 1.5x expected burn); expansion steps: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 24-72h observation windows; automatic rollback if burn-rate > 3x baseline or P99 regressions exceed tolerances.
Adaptive actions enumerated: soft-throttle (reduce concurrency), route to fallback model variant, pause rollout, or alert SRE; triggers and runbook links included.
Dashboards and alerting config templates added to Confluence with links and example Grafana queries; on-call playbook created for both canary and global degradations.
Stakeholder sign-off captured (PM, Eng leads, Observability owner) and a follow-up implementation ticket created for infra/console integrations.

risks_and_open_questions: KV cache and prefix caching can mask tail latencies during canary windows — need synthetic workload to validate canary assumptions.
How to attribute latency violations caused by downstream dependencies (registry, embedding store) — require dependency tagging or shared error budget rules.
Per-tenant burst behavior: what isolation level (soft vs hard) do we enforce when tenant exhausts error budget? Decision needed from product/legal for customer communication.
